purpose: Date-range picker. A trigger button opens a popover that holds a month grid, Start/End date + time fields (suppressible with `show-fields`), an optional timezone selector, and an Apply action; it also offers a "Select Period" mode whose hint chips and typed text are read in the active locale (`45m`, `12 hours` / `12 horas`, `last month` / `mês passado`, `yesterday` / `ontem`, `1/1 - 1/2`). When consumer-provided `presets` are supplied, the trigger splits into two side-by-side segments — a preset dropdown (left, `🕐 <label> ⌄`) that applies a preset range in one click, and the calendar (right, `📅 <range>`) that opens the grid for fine-tuning. Selection is staged in a draft inside the popover and committed to `v-model` only on Apply (or immediately when `show-apply` is false); a preset commits immediately. In period mode, once a span is applied the trigger shows the same two-segment shape — the relative token (e.g. `45m`) beside the concrete window it resolves to (e.g. `14:44 – 23:59`) — since a period selects a time interval rather than whole days. Date math uses the native `Date` API only — no date library; timezone is a selectable IANA label used for display formatting via `Intl` (the picker does not re-interpret `Date` objects across zones).
useWhen: Picking a date range for analytics, logs, or billing windows, optionally with times and a timezone.
Offering one-click ranges ("Last 7 days") next to the grid through `presets`.
Relative time windows typed as text (`45m`, `last month`) with `period`.
avoidWhen: Only a fixed list of named windows, with no custom range → use `select`.
A duration or count (retention days, TTL) rather than a date → use `number-input`.
related: select` — a fixed list of named periods without a grid.
input` — the trigger and the Start/End fields share its heights, hover, and disabled treatment, so they align side by side.
number-input` — numeric durations instead of dates.
bestPractices: modelValue` is committed only on Apply; read the final value from `update:modelValue` or the second argument of `apply`, and set `:show-apply="false"` when every edit should commit at once.
Bind a `{ start, end }` object in range mode and a `Date` or `null` with `mode="single"`.
Bound the selectable days with `min` and `max` instead of validating after commit.
Pair `show-timezone` with `v-model:timezone`; the timezone changes display formatting only, not the `Date` values.
Prefer the `presets` prop; use the `presets` slot with `Calendar.Preset` only when preset content needs custom markup.
